target_customer: Small and mid-sized companies in Mexico, later across Latin America, that run payroll and HR
problem: Mexican payroll involves complex tax and social security rules and government filings that SMEs handled with spreadsheets or accountants. Runa automates payroll calculation, filings and HR tasks in the cloud.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced per employee, with payroll, HR, benefits and time tracking modules
product_category: Payroll and HR software for Latin America

founders.name: Courtney McColgan
founders.background_notes: LatamList (June 22, 2018) calls her the former CMO of Cabify. The only founder listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll engines must encode Mexican tax, social security and labor rules and integrate with government systems, which is detailed but standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll data and compliance logic create switching costs, and local regulatory expertise is a barrier for foreign vendors, but local rivals could build similar software.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found shows an incumbent copying or buying Runa. It kept expanding, announcing Brazil plans in 2021 and reportedly entering Chile, Peru and Colombia in 2025 per Wikipedia.

market_need_then: The founder moved to Peru and worked at Cabify before starting Runa, per the company's press page. Salesforce Ventures made its first Latin America investment in Runa in 2018, indicating investor interest in SME software in the region.

brand_strength.rationale: A short, easy name with an HR suffix in the domain, but no sourced evidence of brand pull beyond customer review scores claimed on its own site.

outcome_analysis: Runa has stayed active, with a 2018 Salesforce Ventures-led seed, a 2019 Series A led by Ribbit Capital and an unverified 2022 Series B, and claims of over 3,500 companies in Mexico on its own site. It expanded beyond Mexico from 2021. Public detail on revenue and rounds is thin and trackers disagree on totals, so the strength of traction is inferred from funding and customer claims.
notes: Founded year: YC says 2018; a Wikipedia mirror says 2017. A Series B of $31M in 2022-11 with total $61.4M appears only on StartupIntros so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Totals conflict: $50.4M, $65.1M and CB Insights $3.62M. Series A amount is not stated in the cited sources. The Series A comes from a Seedtable page plus a profile snippet naming Ribbit Capital; no press release was opened.
